Define single-cell replication initiation zones

Source: R/izones.R
define_initiation_zones.Rd

Cluster single-cell replication tracks into initiation zones (IZs) seeded by replication-timing peaks (e.g. find_rt_peaks() on count_track_centers() output). Per chromosome, tracks are processed from short to long. Tracks flagged as bounded by a gap (flag != 0) or longer than max_track_length are skipped. Each track, widened by 2.5 * bin_size on both sides, either seeds a new putative IZ, joins the single putative IZ it overlaps (by more than min_overlap, plus one bin for tracks longer than short_track_th; if two are overlapped the one with a compatible track-centre interval is used), or is skipped (more than two overlaps, a track of the same cell already in the IZ, or incompatible centres). Short tracks update the putative IZ interval. Putative IZs supported by fewer than min_usage tracks are removed, all tracks are reassigned once more, and IZs with fewer than min_usage reassigned tracks are removed.

Usage

define_initiation_zones(
  tracks,
  rt_peaks,
  short_track_th = "500Kb",
  max_track_length = "1Mb",
  min_overlap = "0bp",
  min_usage = 3L,
  bin_size = "20Kb",
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam(),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

tracks

Named GRangesList of tracks (one element per cell, unique names) with a flag metadata column (e.g. define_replication_tracks()).

rt_peaks

GRanges of seed peaks.

short_track_th

Tracks up to this length define IZ widths.

max_track_length

Longer tracks are not used.

min_overlap

Minimum overlap between a widened track and an IZ.

min_usage

Minimum number of supporting tracks of an IZ (default 3; lower it for small datasets).

bin_size

Bin size of the tracks.

BPPARAM

A BiocParallel::BiocParallelParam; chromosomes are processed in parallel.

verbose

Logical; print progress messages. Default FALSE.

Value

A list with tracks (input tracks with an iz_id metadata column, NA if unassigned) and izones (sorted GRanges with iz_id, q5, q25, q50, q75, q95 and n_tracks).

Details

Each final IZ spans the 5%-95% quantiles of its track centres padded by half a bin on each side (the "fixed" version: start = round(q5 - bin_size / 2), width = q95 - q5 + bin_size). IZs are numbered by genomic order.

Lengths can be given as numbers (bp) or strings such as "500Kb", "1Mb", "0bp".
